title: POC scoping: open-model shortlist & benchmarks - HelioCare Diagnostics
next_steps: Jamie to send 3-model shortlist + preliminary perf/cost matrix by 2026-11-15
Ravi to schedule a 2-hour benchmark slot and provide test harness by 2026-11-18
HelioCare to share 1 week of de-identified sample transcripts and success criteria doc by 2026-11-16
action_items: Jamie Lee: Send pricing & model cost estimates by 2026-11-15
Ravi Patel: Prepare benchmark runner (k6 + Redwood harness) and perf template by 2026-11-18
Priya Desai (HelioCare): Share anonymized dataset and key success metrics by 2026-11-16
summary: Initial POC scoping for a clinical note summarization and triage assistant. Discussed model shortlist tradeoffs (quality vs cost/latency), multilingual requirements (EN + PT-BR), privacy constraints (PHI, on-prem preference), throughput sizing (~30 reqs/s peak), and benchmark plan/timeline.
topics: deployment options: hosted vs private VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Lee: alright everyone hi thanks for joining, we got a full table today, i'm jamie from Redwood AE and ravi's our se. um quick intro round?
[00:07] Dr. Mira Santos: Mira here, head of ai at HelioCare, we own the triage and summarization roadmap.
[00:12] Evan Cole: Evan platform eng, i'll run the infra for the poc.
[00:16] Priya Desai: Priya, product manager, focusing on success metrics and timelines.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: hi all, ravi from redwood se, i'll own the benchmark flow and perf questions.
[00:25] Jamie Lee: cool, agenda: figure out what counts as success, size the workload, pick 2-3 open models to trial, timeline and next steps.
[00:33] Priya Desai: our main use case is clinician note summarization and a triage signal to flag urgent notes. also needs to handle portuguese for our Sao Paulo site.
[00:41] Dr. Mira Santos: correct. accuracy on safety-critical triage is our top metric — false negatives are a big no. second is latency for in-chart realtime, ideally under 600ms p95 but we can budge if quality wins.
[00:55] Evan Cole: infra-wise we can provide 1 GPU worker for initial tests and a small k8s cluster in our dev VPC. we prefer private deployment if possible due to PHI.
[01:06] Jamie Lee: okay noted - PHI and preference for private deployment. we often run a hosted pilot first to iterate faster, but given PHI you may want Redwood Private (VPC). ravi — quick note on network & kms?
[01:17] Ravi Patel: yes we support customer VPC peering and HSM/KMS integrations; for the poc we can do a private control plane with customer-managed keys or work in a pseudo-onprem mode where data never leaves your VPC. will send architecture diagram.
[01:30] Priya Desai: timeline - we want a 4 week POC: week1 data & baseline, week2 run benchmarks, week3 regression checks and quality tuning, week4 decision + exec summary. is that realistic?
[01:41] Ravi Patel: yeah that maps well. if we have your sample data by monday we can kick off benchmark runner day 2. our typical bench run is 24-48h to get stable numbers across latency and throughput.
[01:52] Dr. Mira Santos: about models — we prefer open models for licensing. what would you recommend for clinical highlight/triage and multilingual?
[02:00] Jamie Lee: based on similar customers we propose a shortlist of 3 distinct tradeoffs: a high-quality dense model (e.g., Llama-3-large-ish family or an open LLM tuned mix), a quantized efficient model for latency/cost (eg ggml/4-bit variants), and a multilingual specialty model that handles PT-BR. we will call out specific names in the email.
[02:18] Priya Desai: can you clarify quality deltas? like if the faster model drops F1 by 5-7% is that acceptable?
[02:25] Ravi Patel: we'll measure precision/recall and a triage F1 on your labelled set. we often see cost-optimized quantized models losing 3-10% on specialized clinical tasks vs a fine-tuned dense baseline. tradeoff depends on your tolerance — sounds like safety matters more so we might bias selection to higher quality.
[02:40] Evan Cole: throughput: expected average is 10 rps, peak 30 rps during shift changes. payload size ~1-1.5k tokens per request when we include full note context. how do batching and kv cache affect latency with that pattern?
[02:53] Ravi Patel: good question. Redwood can do continuous batching with soft latency SLOs; on average 10 rps with 1.5k tokens you're mostly bound by model decode time. kv/prefix cache helps if many requests share similar history — for note summarization less reuse but we can cache template prompts. we will run experiments with and without batching.
[03:08] Jamie Lee: cost ballpark - rough numbers: hosted smaller models might be $0.05-$0.12 per 1k tokens, larger tuned baselines $0.20-$0.5 per 1k tokens; dedicated/private contracts change economics. we'll provide a cost matrix per model.
[03:24] Priya Desai: security checklist — we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO (SAML), RBAC, and KMS integration. also data residency in brazil for certain records.
[03:33] Ravi Patel: we have SOC2, SSO and SAML support, per-token traceability and audit logs in Redwood Console. for data residency we can deploy nodes in GCP sao paulo region or run customer-provided on-prem.
[03:46] Dr. Mira Santos: about evaluation: we need both automated metrics (F1 for triage, ROUGE for summaries?) and clinician-in-the-loop qualitative scoring. can you run blind A/B on outputs?
[03:57] Ravi Patel: yes, bench harness supports A/B comparisons and we can produce side-by-side outputs plus token-level latencies. we'll also export results as CSV for your clinicians to rate.
[04:08] Evan Cole: network/firewall — we'll need a requirements doc for ports and peering.
[04:12] Jamie Lee: i'll put that in the follow up along with the architecture diagram.
[04:15] Priya Desai: is there any specific infra we need for multilingual? like tokenizer issues with PT-BR?
[04:20] Ravi Patel: mainly model selection — some models are trained multi-lingual and handle PT-BR gracefully; tokenizer mismatch can cause token bloat but we'll quantify tokens/test. we'll include tokenization stats in the bench.
[04:29] Dr. Mira Santos: do you have examples where open models matched closed-source on clinical tasks?
[04:33] Ravi Patel: yes in a few medtech POCs we saw open models with task-specific fine-tuning (or LoRA) close the gap to closed models for NER/summarization; but they required domain-tuning and extra eval sets.
[04:44] Jamie Lee: ok let's line up the model shortlist for the email: 1) high-quality dense baseline (open LLM w/ clinical tuning), 2) quantized latency-optimized model (4-bit; low cost), 3) multilingual/pt-br candidate (multilingual open model). we'll rank them on expected quality, latency, and cost.
[04:58] Priya Desai: perfect. what about rollout strategy after POC if we pick private? can we canary to a subset of clinicians?
[05:04] Ravi Patel: yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a simpler model if latency spikes or error rate increases.
[05:13] Dr. Mira Santos: any blockers from your side to start once we share sample data?
[05:17] Ravi Patel: none. main blockers: receiving de-identified dataset and a list of success metric thresholds. also access for our bench runner to your dev VPC or a sample upload location.
[05:28] Jamie Lee: recap & next steps: Jamie sends 3-model shortlist + perf/cost template + security docs; Ravi sends benchmark harness and architecture diagram and schedules the run; HelioCare shares anonymized dataset and success criteria. target to start bench by 2026-11-18.
[05:44] Priya Desai: sounds good. thanks all.
[05:46] Dr. Mira Santos: thanks.
[05:48] Jamie Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the email and actions. bye.
[05:52] [call ended]
